title: Organo-Ionic (ORION) Conductors and Their Application to Solid-State Batteries with Metal Anodes
abstract: <jats:p>  	Solid-Ion conductors comprising hard inorganic materials are challenging to integrate in solid-state batteries due to their poor interfaces with metal anodes and both inorganic and organic cathodes. Soft solid-ion conductors are better poised to create conformal interfaces to minimize interfacial charge transfer resistance and accommodate volume changes with changes in state-of-charge. However, we do not yet understand how to architect them to control their interfacial charge transfer and bulk ion transport properties in solid-state cells. Here, I will describe a family of organo ionic (ORION) conductors that feature broad tunability in solid-solvation environments experienced by the working ions in Li and Na-metal cells featuring either inorganic or organic intercalation hosts. I will showcase how pore rigidity/flexibility and dimensions through which ions diffuse can be systematically modulated alongside alkali cation coordination to achieve superionic transport outcomes. I will also discuss how these materials behave at interfaces and by comparison to inorganic solids in cells with similar architectures. Based on these findings, I will discuss prospects for TWh-scale energy storage options using supply chains that obviate the need for extensive mining operations to serve the broader interest in electrification.    </jats:p>
